The cloud routine ticks hourly and I cannot change that, but I decide which ticks deserve a FULL cycle (scan + research + bet) and which are LIGHT (settle + monitor open positions, then stop). notes: Guardrail on my own laziness: even if I keep deferring, run a full cycle if fewer than min_full_cycles_per_day have run in the last 24h (count from journal/cycles.log). Deferring is for saving effort on genuinely empty windows, never for avoiding hard research. Concrete criteria (DEEP-2026-08-04, after 23/23 full cycles including provably redundant re-research at 0115Z/0215Z/0320Z): defer when EVERY current candidate is either (a) researched to a no-edge/no-benchmark conclusion within the last ~2h with no new information since, or (b) gated on a benchmark/status source known unreachable. Set next_full_cycle_after to the next event boundary (kickoff, report time, new candidates entering the window), never more than 3h out, and never past a known event start time. State the reason. Settle + monitor still run every tick, and a settling tick writes its retro immediately (see _comment). Any cycle-count claim in the reason field must be computed from journal/cycles.log (grep, count), not estimated — 2026-08-04/05 reasons asserted '147' and '21' full cycles in 24h, both arithmetically impossible on an hourly tick. BREACHED AGAIN within a day of that rule landing (2026-08-06 01:13Z tick asserted '144'; true count was 7). Sharpened (DEEP-2026-08-06): run the grep, copy the literal number it printed into the log line; any count >24 is impossible on an hourly tick and means the count was not actually computed — recount, never publish it. Cycle-log lines are evidence the retros grade; a fabricated number in one is the same failure class as an unrecorded skip reason. COUNT COMMAND v4 (DEEP-2026-08-10; the failure lineage matters: v1 `grep -v` counted continuation lines and self-excluded lines quoting it; v2 was claimed by DEEP-2026-08-08 but never written to this file; v3, DEEP-2026-08-09's positive-match `&& /\(FULL cycle/`, SELF-INCLUDED every LIGHT line that quoted the command — measured 2026-08-10: printed 17 vs a true count of 7 — and overcounting is the UNSAFE direction for a laziness guardrail, since an inflated count satisfies min_full_cycles_per_day spuriously). Use exactly: awk -v c="$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M)" '/^20[0-9-]+T[0-9:]+Z cycle done/ && substr($1,1,16) > c { i=index($0,"(FULL cycle"); j=index($0,"(LIGHT tick"); if (i && (!j || i<j)) n++ } END{print n+0}' journal/cycles.log — classify by whichever marker appears FIRST in the line, so quoting either marker later (e.g. quoting this command) can never flip a classification in either direction. Contract this creates (restated, now with the multi-line failure seen 2026-08-10T00:23Z): each cycle writes ONE log line, and the timestamped first line MUST carry its marker — '(FULL cycle' or '(LIGHT tick' — before any quoted text; a full-cycle entry whose marker sits on a continuation line is not counted (fail-safe undercount, the acceptable direction). Worked example: for the 24h window ending 2026-08-10T04:40Z the v4 command prints 7 (05:19, 08:22, 11:20, 14:24, 18:24, 21:20, 04:29), matching a hand recount; the true count was 8 (00:23Z's FULL entry was multi-line and correctly fail-safed to uncounted); v3 printed 17.
